approach.method_basis: Simulated annealing keeps one current configuration, perturbs it randomly, and always accepts an improvement while accepting a deterioration with a probability that falls as a temperature parameter cools. Early on the walk can move downhill and escape a local optimum; late on it behaves almost greedily. approach.novelty: This root runs many independent walks in parallel rather than one, with at most one outstanding proposal per walk, so the oracle batch is filled by different points in the space instead of by one trajectory. It ties the cooling schedule to accumulated feedback rather than wall time, seeds the initial temperature from the spread of the initial scores, and keeps a separate best-observed archive so that accepting a downhill move never loses the incumbent.

hypothesis: Maintain independent task-local molecular graph walks, generate de novo atom or bond edits from each current working state, accept nondecreasing observed scores and accept decreases with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), and cool T as accepted feedback accumulates while preserving a separate best-observed archive.

finding_summary.headline: The annealing machinery was exact in every respect and produced the round's lowest score, 0.233
finding_summary.insights: This node isolates the round's most important lesson. The search algorithm is provably correct and the search still failed, so what separates the field is not the optimizer but the proposal distribution it draws from. Aromatic content here is 50 to 67 percent against 87 to 100 percent for every root above 0.4, and the graph edits repeatedly produce aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres that are not real chemistry. Any future work on this lineage belongs in the edit operator set, not in the acceptance rule or the cooling schedule. One seed only, and its deco_hop result shows the walk does work where the initial molecules are already close.
finding_summary.results: This is the weakest of the thirteen roots at 0.233. It reached 0.558 on deco_hop and 0.382 on zaleplon_mpo but collapsed to 0.045 on drd2_docking and 0.014 on sitagliptin_mpo, where the median score across all 290 proposals was zero. Every mechanism check was exact: the recomputed cooling schedule agreed with all 145 proposal temperatures and all 1,450 stored proposal temperatures, the Metropolis decision reproduced 1,450 times out of 1,450 including the logged uniform variates, 557 downhill moves were accepted and 546 of them were genuinely reused as the source of a later proposal, and the best archive matched an independent cumulative maximum at all 1,600 checkpoints.

molecular.headline: Aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres: a correct search over chemistry that does not exist
molecular.overall_character: Ring closure is high at 97 percent on every objective, but only half to two thirds of proposals contain any ordinary aromatic atom, the lowest of any root that completed. The gap is filled by exotic ring systems the graph editor is willing to construct: phosphinine rings written with aromatic phosphorus, hypervalent phosphorus and sulfur centres, and nitrogen-halogen bonds. These appear not only in the failures but in the highest-scoring molecule on two objectives, which means the oracle is scoring structures that could not be made. Molecules average sixty to sixty-four characters throughout, with no size control varying by objective.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals average sixty characters with 60 percent aromatic content. The best molecules are thiourea-containing pyrazolines decorated with phosphinine rings, written with lowercase aromatic phosphorus.

cyclic thioureas are reactive and metabolically unstable
missing_features: carbon-only aromatic rings in place of the phosphorus-containing ones

transferable_gaps.evidence: Phosphinine rings written with lowercase aromatic phosphorus appear in all four highest-scoring molecules on one objective and among the low scorers on another, and hypervalent phosphorus appears in the top molecule of a third.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator constructs rings containing aromatic phosphorus
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The atom substitution alphabet admits phosphorus into aromatic ring positions where valence rules permit it, producing structures that are formally parseable and chemically fictional. Restricting aromatic ring membership to the elements that actually form drug-like aromatics would close this off.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring proposals on two objectives carry N-Br and N-Cl bonds directly, produced by ordinary atom substitution on amine nitrogens.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator forms nitrogen-halogen and oxygen-halogen bonds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Bond formation is checked for valence but not for whether the bond is chemically viable, so a legal edit produces a reagent rather than a candidate. A bond-level stability filter at emission would remove these at no cost to the walk.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cooling schedule, the Metropolis acceptance and the incumbent archive all reproduced exactly on all 1,450 transitions, with 546 of 557 accepted downhill moves genuinely reused, and the result was still the lowest score of the round.
transferable_gaps.gap: a provably correct search cannot compensate for an unusable proposal distribution
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Effort spent on the acceptance rule, the temperature schedule, or the number of parallel walks cannot help while half the proposals fall outside real chemistry. The edit operator set is the only thing worth changing on this lineage.

method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.

applicability_conditions: Applies to independent scalar molecular maximization tasks with usable scored initial molecular graphs and a sufficiently broad valid graph-edit neighborhood.

The useful-barrier hypothesis requires that some temporarily worse structures lead to later improvements within the available feedback; the supplied evidence does not establish that prerequisite for this lineage.

Temperature is calibrated only from the current objective's initial observations, and schedule progress uses the remaining budget announced through the protocol. The positive floor makes behavior on nearly equal initial scores explicit.
Each parallel walk has at most one outstanding proposal, so every acceptance decision compares a scored neighbor with its true source state without batching-order ambiguity.

Validity and novelty filtering make the effective graph proposal asymmetric and history dependent. This is a finite-budget optimization heuristic, with no claim of equilibrium sampling, detailed balance or asymptotic annealing convergence.
Only accepted observations from the current process affect transitions or the archive; no corpus molecule retrieval, task-specific chemistry branch or shared labeled state is permitted.

Root screening evidence cannot establish multi-seed reliability. Posterior-sampled lookahead from the method proposal is reserved for a later experiment conditioned on measured long or unproductive real-evaluation excursions.

research_intent.falsifier: The annealing mechanism is refuted if proposal sources do not follow their own recorded working states, acceptance probabilities or random decisions disagree with the declared observed-score rule, temperatures do not cool with accepted feedback, a lower accepted state is discarded in favor of a ranked or archive-selected replacement, or any emitted molecule lacks de novo graph-edit provenance. Archive loss or task-crossing labels violate the declared invariants. Complete trajectories with no realized downhill acceptance or no later editing from an accepted downhill state do not establish the exploratory component; report it as unactivated on that run, and distinguish insufficient downhill opportunities or end-of-budget censoring from an incorrect implementation. Missing diagnostics make activation inconclusive. Failure to produce full valid novel batches refutes generative viability. Once the state transitions and downhill followthrough activate, failure to recover losses or improve final Top-1 remains negative score evidence rather than an execution failure.
research_intent.implementation_change: Implement an import-safe optimize.py with a preparation command that publishes reusable graph-operator and cooling configuration only, without reading labels or retaining corpus molecules. The run command uses RDKit graphs and starts persistent walks from the supplied valid scored initial structures. Create enough independently tracked walks to assign at most one outstanding proposal per walk in each batch; cycle the initial structures if more walks than supplied structures are needed. Schedule walks round-robin using the batch size announced in init. Seed all used RNGs from init and keep every observation and working state local to that objective process. Set an initial temperature from the supplied initial-score dispersion with a positive floor, then use a fixed geometric schedule ending at one twentieth of the initial temperature as accepted new evaluations consume the initial announced remaining budget. Freeze and log those schedule parameters before proposing. Generate each neighbor through randomized atom/bond additions, removals, replacements or bond-order/connectivity edits of its assigned walk state. Sanitize and canonicalize locally, rejecting invalid and globally or batch-duplicate identities. Retry from the same scored working state, allowing a short composed graph-edit proposal when needed for novelty; any unscored intermediate graph remains proposal construction and never becomes a persistent walk state. Generate enough fresh neighbors to emit exactly the announced suggestion count. Store each emitted identity with its walk id, source identity, source score, operator trace and proposal-time temperature. On accepted feedback, compare the observed score with that exact source snapshot. Accept nonnegative score differences with probability one; for negative differences use exp(delta/T) and an independent uniform draw. A rejected transition retains its source state. Later proposals must edit the resulting accepted state even when it is worse than an earlier state or the best archive entry. Preserve the cumulative best observed molecule in a separate archive that never replaces the walks or supplies ranked breeding parents. Apply the maximization acceptance rule from [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf); the molecular edits, finite cooling schedule and parallel walks are this root's implementation choices. Emit structured stderr diagnostics for initialization, temperatures and budget progress, every graph-generation attempt, source snapshots, acceptance arithmetic and random draws, state transitions, subsequent proposal sources, and archive values. Handle rejected evaluator entries without fabricating labels and exit silently on stop. There is no learned predictor, surrogate-only lookahead, corpus candidate pool, crossover, greedy population survival, archive restart or cross-task state in this root.
research_intent.mechanism: Maintain independent task-local molecular graph walks, generate de novo atom or bond edits from each current working state, accept nondecreasing observed scores and accept decreases with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), and cool T as accepted feedback accumulates while preserving a separate best-observed archive.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: This lineage has no Parent or evaluated annealing root. A short task-local molecular search can stall when each improving structure requires an intermediate edit with a lower observed score. The supplied evidence for other paradigms does not establish that such barriers occur, or that crossing them pays off within this benchmark. This root tests persistent score-conditioned graph trajectories that can continue from a temporary loss while preserving the best observed result separately.

applicability_conditions: Activation is supported on seed 0 for all five molecular scalar maximization objectives with ten usable initial graphs, ten persistent walks, batch size ten and 290 additional accepted evaluations per task. No Parent or multi-seed comparison is available.

The graph-edit neighborhood supplies valid novel single-edit neighbors within at most four attempts in this run. All eight operators activate, but the implemented two/three-edit escalation and protocol paths for evaluator rejection or more walks than a batch are untested here.

Temperature is fitted only to each task's initial score dispersion and then follows the frozen twentyfold geometric cooling schedule. The 0.03 initial floor controls deco_hop, drd2_docking and sitagliptin_mpo. For sitagliptin_mpo, 158 of 161 downhill proposals are accepted and only two accepted losses have magnitude at least 0.001; matched-loss cooling is nevertheless verified independently of encountered loss sizes.

Every realized downhill state with remaining feedback opportunity is used in a later proposal. Recovery above the pre-loss score is observed for 328/557 excursions; 229 remain unrecovered, including eleven final-step excursions without a followup opportunity. No controlled comparison establishes whether allowing losses improves final Top-1.

The archive preserves all observed maxima even when all working states drift below it. median_2 retains its initial Top-1 without improvement, and only seven excursions have subsequent same-walk archive improvements. These are bounded score outcomes and do not negate confirmed execution.

Validity and historical novelty filtering yield asymmetric, history-dependent proposal distributions. The supported behavior is finite-budget optimization, with no equilibrium, detailed-balance or asymptotic-convergence claim.

The reusable artifact contains configuration only; all labels, working states, proposals, acceptance RNG state and archive records restart per objective. No corpus retrieval, surrogate, lookahead, crossover, ranked replacement or archive restart is present.

molecular_assessment.headline: Aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres: a correct search over chemistry that does not exist
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Ring closure is high at 97 percent on every objective, but only half to two thirds of proposals contain any ordinary aromatic atom, the lowest of any root that completed. The gap is filled by exotic ring systems the graph editor is willing to construct: phosphinine rings written with aromatic phosphorus, hypervalent phosphorus and sulfur centres, and nitrogen-halogen bonds. These appear not only in the failures but in the highest-scoring molecule on two objectives, which means the oracle is scoring structures that could not be made. Molecules average sixty to sixty-four characters throughout, with no size control varying by objective.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals average sixty characters with 60 percent aromatic content. The best molecules are thiourea-containing pyrazolines decorated with phosphinine rings, written with lowercase aromatic phosphorus.
liabilities: aromatic phosphorus rings appear in all four top-scoring molecules
cyclic thioureas are reactive and metabolically unstable
missing_features: carbon-only aromatic rings in place of the phosphorus-containing ones
molecules distributed across the score range rather than clustered at one point and at zero
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The median across 290 proposals is one in a million, so almost the whole budget bought nothing, while the top four cluster tightly between 0.360 and 0.382 on one thiosemicarbazide scaffold. The walk found one narrow region and the rest of the space was empty.

per_task.generated_character: The node's best objective at 0.558. Substituted indole and quinolinone carboxamides averaging sixty-one characters with 66 percent aromatic content, the highest on this node.
liabilities: nitrogen-bromine and nitrogen-chlorine bonds in the low scorers are not stable
N-alkoxyamine groups appear throughout the top scorers and are unusual in drug molecules
missing_features: consistent ring content, with a tail of acyclic halogenated alkanes at the bottom
per_task.score_gradient_reading: This is the one objective where the population looks like chemistry, and it is also the one where the node performs acceptably. The top scorers are fluorochlorophenyl amides on hydroxylated indoles; the bottom of the range is occupied by small halogenated alkanes with no ring at all.

per_task.generated_character: The weakest drd2_docking result in the round by a wide margin. Proposals average sixty-four characters with only 52 percent carrying an ordinary aromatic atom, and the top scorers are built on hypervalent phosphorus rings fused to bridged aminal cages.
liabilities: hypervalent phosphorus written as PH inside a ring is not a stable species
aromatic phosphorus rings appear in the low scorers and are not drug chemistry
bridged aminal cages with adjacent nitrogen and oxygen would hydrolyse immediately
missing_features: a protonatable aliphatic amine on an ordinary aromatic scaffold
simple fused bicyclic aromatics such as indole or tetrahydroisoquinoline
any molecule at all in the size and polarity range that scores well on this objective
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The entire population spans 0.0004 to 0.045, so there is effectively no gradient to climb. For comparison, two other roots reached above 0.9 on this objective by finding a basic amine on a simple fused aromatic; nothing resembling that appears anywhere in this population.

per_task.generated_character: Ethyl benzoate esters carrying a dimethyl pyrimidinedione, averaging sixty characters with 67 percent aromatic content, the highest on this node, and 97 percent ring closure.
liabilities: nitrogen-bromine bonds in the low scorers are reagents, not candidates
thiol substituents on saturated carbons oxidise readily
missing_features: consistent aromatic content, with a third of proposals carrying none
molecules positioned between the two similarity targets rather than near one
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best reaches 0.159 against a median of 0.110, one of the tighter bands on this node. The top scorers are the only proposals that look like ordinary heteroaromatic chemistry; the bottom is occupied by small halogenated alkanes carrying N-Br bonds.

per_task.generated_character: The weakest set on the node and in the round. Exactly half of proposals carry an aromatic atom, averaging sixty-three characters of fused esters and hypervalent phosphorus and sulfur heterocycles.
liabilities: hypervalent sulfur and phosphorus written as SH and PH inside rings
strained bridged aminals with adjacent nitrogen and oxygen
missing_features: aromatic rings, absent from half the population
fluorinated aliphatic chemistry, which barely appears
any molecule scoring above 0.02 across the whole budget
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best is 0.0137 and the median is exactly zero, so the entire 290-call budget produced nothing usable. Even the top molecule is a strained fused lactone rather than anything resembling a candidate for this objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Phosphinine rings written with lowercase aromatic phosphorus appear in all four highest-scoring molecules on one objective and among the low scorers on another, and hypervalent phosphorus appears in the top molecule of a third.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator constructs rings containing aromatic phosphorus
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The atom substitution alphabet admits phosphorus into aromatic ring positions where valence rules permit it, producing structures that are formally parseable and chemically fictional. Restricting aromatic ring membership to the elements that actually form drug-like aromatics would close this off.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring proposals on two objectives carry N-Br and N-Cl bonds directly, produced by ordinary atom substitution on amine nitrogens.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator forms nitrogen-halogen and oxygen-halogen bonds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Bond formation is checked for valence but not for whether the bond is chemically viable, so a legal edit produces a reagent rather than a candidate. A bond-level stability filter at emission would remove these at no cost to the walk.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cooling schedule, the Metropolis acceptance and the incumbent archive all reproduced exactly on all 1,450 transitions, with 546 of 557 accepted downhill moves genuinely reused, and the result was still the lowest score of the round.
transferable_gaps.gap: a provably correct search cannot compensate for an unusable proposal distribution
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Effort spent on the acceptance rule, the temperature schedule, or the number of parallel walks cannot help while half the proposals fall outside real chemistry. The edit operator set is the only thing worth changing on this lineage.

applicability_conditions: Applies to independent scalar molecular maximization tasks with usable scored initial molecular graphs and a sufficiently broad valid graph-edit neighborhood.

The useful-barrier hypothesis requires that some temporarily worse structures lead to later improvements within the available feedback; the supplied evidence does not establish that prerequisite for this lineage.

Temperature is calibrated only from the current objective's initial observations, and schedule progress uses the remaining budget announced through the protocol. The positive floor makes behavior on nearly equal initial scores explicit.
Each parallel walk has at most one outstanding proposal, so every acceptance decision compares a scored neighbor with its true source state without batching-order ambiguity.

Validity and novelty filtering make the effective graph proposal asymmetric and history dependent. This is a finite-budget optimization heuristic, with no claim of equilibrium sampling, detailed balance or asymptotic annealing convergence.
Only accepted observations from the current process affect transitions or the archive; no corpus molecule retrieval, task-specific chemistry branch or shared labeled state is permitted.

Root screening evidence cannot establish multi-seed reliability. Posterior-sampled lookahead from the method proposal is reserved for a later experiment conditioned on measured long or unproductive real-evaluation excursions.

approach.method_basis: Simulated annealing keeps one current configuration, perturbs it randomly, and always accepts an improvement while accepting a deterioration with a probability that falls as a temperature parameter cools. Early on the walk can move downhill and escape a local optimum; late on it behaves almost greedily. Applied to molecules, the configuration is a graph, the perturbation is an atom or bond edit, and the acceptance test uses the observed score returned by the oracle.
approach.novelty: This root runs many independent walks in parallel rather than one, with at most one outstanding proposal per walk, so the oracle batch is filled by different points in the space instead of by one trajectory. It ties the cooling schedule to accumulated feedback rather than wall time, seeds the initial temperature from the spread of the initial scores, and keeps a separate best-observed archive so that accepting a downhill move never loses the incumbent.

research_intent.falsifier: The annealing mechanism is refuted if proposal sources do not follow their own recorded working states, acceptance probabilities or random decisions disagree with the declared observed-score rule, temperatures do not cool with accepted feedback, a lower accepted state is discarded in favor of a ranked or archive-selected replacement, or any emitted molecule lacks de novo graph-edit provenance. Archive loss or task-crossing labels violate the declared invariants. Complete trajectories with no realized downhill acceptance or no later editing from an accepted downhill state do not establish the exploratory component; report it as unactivated on that run, and distinguish insufficient downhill opportunities or end-of-budget censoring from an incorrect implementation. Missing diagnostics make activation inconclusive. Failure to produce full valid novel batches refutes generative viability. Once the state transitions and downhill followthrough activate, failure to recover losses or improve final Top-1 remains negative score evidence rather than an execution failure.
research_intent.implementation_change: Implement an import-safe optimize.py with a preparation command that publishes reusable graph-operator and cooling configuration only, without reading labels or retaining corpus molecules. The run command uses RDKit graphs and starts persistent walks from the supplied valid scored initial structures. Create enough independently tracked walks to assign at most one outstanding proposal per walk in each batch; cycle the initial structures if more walks than supplied structures are needed. Schedule walks round-robin using the batch size announced in init. Seed all used RNGs from init and keep every observation and working state local to that objective process. Set an initial temperature from the supplied initial-score dispersion with a positive floor, then use a fixed geometric schedule ending at one twentieth of the initial temperature as accepted new evaluations consume the initial announced remaining budget. Freeze and log those schedule parameters before proposing. Generate each neighbor through randomized atom/bond additions, removals, replacements or bond-order/connectivity edits of its assigned walk state. Sanitize and canonicalize locally, rejecting invalid and globally or batch-duplicate identities. Retry from the same scored working state, allowing a short composed graph-edit proposal when needed for novelty; any unscored intermediate graph remains proposal construction and never becomes a persistent walk state. Generate enough fresh neighbors to emit exactly the announced suggestion count. Store each emitted identity with its walk id, source identity, source score, operator trace and proposal-time temperature. On accepted feedback, compare the observed score with that exact source snapshot. Accept nonnegative score differences with probability one; for negative differences use exp(delta/T) and an independent uniform draw. A rejected transition retains its source state. Later proposals must edit the resulting accepted state even when it is worse than an earlier state or the best archive entry. Preserve the cumulative best observed molecule in a separate archive that never replaces the walks or supplies ranked breeding parents. Apply the maximization acceptance rule from [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf); the molecular edits, finite cooling schedule and parallel walks are this root's implementation choices. Emit structured stderr diagnostics for initialization, temperatures and budget progress, every graph-generation attempt, source snapshots, acceptance arithmetic and random draws, state transitions, subsequent proposal sources, and archive values. Handle rejected evaluator entries without fabricating labels and exit silently on stop. There is no learned predictor, surrogate-only lookahead, corpus candidate pool, crossover, greedy population survival, archive restart or cross-task state in this root.
research_intent.mechanism: Maintain independent task-local molecular graph walks, generate de novo atom or bond edits from each current working state, accept nondecreasing observed scores and accept decreases with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), and cool T as accepted feedback accumulates while preserving a separate best-observed archive.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: This lineage has no Parent or evaluated annealing root. A short task-local molecular search can stall when each improving structure requires an intermediate edit with a lower observed score. The supplied evidence for other paradigms does not establish that such barriers occur, or that crossing them pays off within this benchmark. This root tests persistent score-conditioned graph trajectories that can continue from a temporary loss while preserving the best observed result separately.
